metadata.name: Liberal feminism
metadata.description: American egalitarian liberal feminism, emphasizing equal rights, personal autonomy and public support for equal opportunity; represented by NOW and liberal feminist scholarship.
metadata.scope: US egalitarian liberal feminism represented by NOW and scholarship. Unsupported extensions beyond the cited programme remain unknown. Government acts are context, not a substitute for evidence of this tradition.
metadata.phrase: A society securing equal civil rights, political participation and practical opportunities for women through legal and institutional reform.

answers.rationale: Regular competitive elections make women equal co-authors of government rather than subjects of permanent rulers.
Expert advice is useful, but substituting an expert panel for citizens denies equal political agency.
Intellectual or educational exclusions would contradict equal citizenship and reproduce unequal opportunities.
Constitutional lawmaking and congressional accountability rule out unilateral executive legislation against parliament.
Competitive opposition is necessary for meaningful and inclusive electoral choice.

Unresolved after independent review: The resolutions support disclosure of the Epstein files and congressional accountability, but do not establish the exact right of opposition representatives to investigate government spending. Transparency in another case is insufficient for this precise institutional claim.
The constitutional civil-rights strategy requires courts able to remedy unlawful governmental decisions.
Union representation cannot replace the equal political voice of citizens outside organised labour.
Government exclusion of opponents by political position undermines equal participation and competitive choice.

Equal citizenship does not establish this particular referendum or recall mechanism. Earlier rationale under review: Binding popular repeal is supported as participation, inferred subject to constitutional equality protections.
The demand for legislative control of executive action contradicts sole national decision authority.
The contemporary programme expressly favours impeachment or resignation as constitutional accountability mechanisms.
A leader deciding when voters may judge them destroys accountable co-authorship of government.

Equal citizenship does not establish this particular referendum or recall mechanism. Earlier rationale under review: Defined recall procedures can extend voter accountability, provided equal participation and due process are preserved.
Unaccountable national leadership directly denies citizens political autonomy.
Military replacement of civilian government bypasses the constitutional democratic processes used to secure equal rights.

answers.rationale: NOW opposes unilateral imperial expansion and the Iraq occupation (Issues Manual pp190–191), while endorsing multinational peacekeeping (pp89–90). This supports qualified disagreement with using force for national interests without an attack, not absolute pacifism.

The adopted feminist foreign-policy campaign expressly prioritises peace and international collaboration, and the 2004 Iraq resolution replaces unilateral occupation with negotiated multinational peacekeeping. Infer a preference for slower diplomatic means rather than a claim no military action is ever legitimate.

Issues Manual pp190–191 explicitly opposes enormous increases in defence spending and prolonged deployment that displace social services. This warrants qualified disagreement with costly superiority, while retaining support for some international peacekeeping forces.

Opposition to unjustified war does not establish this specific operational policy; an exception to opposition is not positive endorsement of force. Earlier rationale under review: The resolution distinguishes an evidenced immediate threat from unsubstantiated aggression, permitting narrowly defensive prevention.

NOW explicitly sought expanded international peacekeeping in Afghanistan and a UN multinational force in Iraq (Issues Manual pp89–90). Those humanitarian missions are not restricted to responding to an attack against the US or an ally, so infer qualified disagreement with the exclusive condition.

The 2021 draft-registration resolution explicitly calls for ending compulsory registration and voluntary service for all people. This is opposition to compulsory service itself, rather than merely a request for equal male and female conscription.

Opposition to unjustified war does not establish this specific operational policy; an exception to opposition is not positive endorsement of force. Earlier rationale under review: Substantial diplomatic concessions can be justified to protect civilians and prevent war, subject to basic rights.

Opposition to unjustified war does not establish this specific operational policy; an exception to opposition is not positive endorsement of force. Earlier rationale under review: Removing human attack approval raises accountability and civilian-protection concerns that efficiency alone does not resolve.
Defensive protection better fits the emphasis on immediate danger than discretionary foreign campaigns.

Support for international peacekeeping and for increasing its personnel in Afghanistan (Issues Manual pp89–90) precludes an absolute prohibition on all military action. This does not establish support for every alliance war.

Unresolved after independent source review: NOW supports some international peacekeeping missions while opposing occupations. Those positions do not settle maintaining national forces capable of prolonged combat overseas; mission purpose and combat capacity are different questions.
Peaceful continuation of a territorial dispute is preferable to initiating war over it.

Opposition to unjustified war does not establish this specific operational policy; an exception to opposition is not positive endorsement of force. Earlier rationale under review: Coercive threats can endanger civilians and displace the preferred diplomatic resolution of disputes.

The adopted foreign-policy campaign prioritises peace and disruption of violent power structures. Together with opposition to militarist expansion in the Issues Manual pp190–191, this warrants a qualified preference for reducing war risks over displays of resolve.

Opposition to unjustified war does not establish this specific operational policy; an exception to opposition is not positive endorsement of force. Earlier rationale under review: Intelligence protecting against an immediate threat can be justified; seeking advantage at the cost of escalation is not a general mandate.

Opposition to unjustified war does not establish this specific operational policy; an exception to opposition is not positive endorsement of force. Earlier rationale under review: Negotiated capability reductions are consistent with peacebuilding if they preserve adequate protection against aggression.
